facts.statement: Brachylophosaurus goodwini is listed as a possible synonym for Probrachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Brachylophosaurus goodwini? Horner, 1988

facts.statement: The dinosaur was first discovered in Montana in 1981 and fully excavated in 2008.
facts.quote: First discovered in Montana in 1981 and not fully excavated until 2008

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus bergei was named and described in 2015 by Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler and Jack Horner.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Probrachylophosaurus bergei was named and described by Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler and Jack Horner.

facts.statement: Fossils of Probrachylophosaurus date to the Campanian age between 80.45 and 79 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in rocks of the Judith River Formation in Montana and the Foremost Formation in Alberta, and date to the Campanian age, 80.45–79 million years ago.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus possessed a short, paddle-shaped head crest formed by an extension of the nasal bone.
facts.quote: In Probrachylophosaurus this crest is a short, paddle-shaped extension of the nasal bone projecting over the back of the head.

facts.statement: Histologic analysis indicates that Probrachylophosaurus experienced fast growth rates similar to other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Histologic analysis indicates fast growth, similar to other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: Comparisons with Maiasaura suggest Probrachylophosaurus took approximately twice as long to reach sexual maturity.
facts.quote: However, comparisons with the related Maiasaura indicate that Probrachylophosaurus took around twice as long to reach sexual maturity.

facts.statement: The oldest known specimen was approximately 14 years old and had reached over 95% of its adult size at death.
facts.quote: The oldest known specimen had likely reached over 95% of its adult size upon death at 14 years of age, but did not yet show signs of complete skeletal maturity.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Brachylophosaurus goodwini might be a younger specimen of Probrachylophosaurus bergei, but poor preservation prevents a definite conclusion.
facts.quote: Therefore, they considered it possible that B. goodwini merely represented a younger specimen of P. bergei. If true, this would make P. bergei a junior synonym of B. goodwini; however, the study refrained from making a definite assignment or taking nomenclatural action due to the poor preservation of "B. goodwini" preventing definite conclusions about its identity.

facts.statement: In 2021, three specimens from the Foremost Formation were assigned to the genus Probrachylophosaurus but not to the species P. bergei.
facts.quote: In 2021, three specimens from the upper layers of the Foremost Formation were referred to the genus Probrachylophosaurus, though not to P. bergei.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus was a large quadrupedal hadrosaur with slender forelimbs, robust hindlimbs, and a long tail stiffened by ossified tendons.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaur, Probrachylophosaurus would have been a large quadrupedal animal with gracile forelimbs, longer more robust hindlimbs, and a long, tall horizontal tail stiffened by ossified tendons.

facts.statement: The estimated length of Probrachylophosaurus is 10 meters.
facts.quote: Its size has been estimated at 10 m in length.

facts.statement: The holotype of Probrachylophosaurus had an estimated body mass of 4.3 metric tonnes at death.
facts.quote: Body mass estimate suggests that the holotype was 4.3 MT at time of death, and was close to maximum size.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is distinguished by a unique combination of traits rather than entirely unique traits, aside from its short, paddle-shaped crest raised in the center.
facts.quote: In addition to its unique crest, which was short, paddle-shaped, and raised in the centre, Probrachylophosaurus can be distinguished by its unique combination of traits (a differential diagnosis) rather than entirely unique traits (autapomorphies).

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus exhibits an intermediate anatomical condition between the earlier crestless Acristavus and its possible descendant Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: In particular, Probrachylophosaurus shows a distinctly intermediate condition between the anatomy of the earlier crestless relative Acristavus and its possible descendant Brachylophosaurus.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus possessed a large beak at the front of its mouth, similar to other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The front of the mouth would have borne a large beak, as in other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: The lower jaw beak of Probrachylophosaurus was formed by a predentary bone that was roughly twice as wide as it was long with squared-off front corners.
facts.quote: On the lower jaw, the beak was formed by the predentary bone, which was roughly twice as wide as long with squared off front corners.

facts.statement: Unlike the flat crest of Brachylophosaurus, the crest of Probrachylophosaurus is raised in the center, forming a triangular cross-section with an angle of 112 degrees in the known adult specimen.
facts.quote: Unlike the relatively flat crest of Brachylophosaurus, that of Probrachylophosaurus is raised in the centre, forming a triangular cross section with the top points forming an angle of less than 130° (112° in the known adult specimen).

facts.statement: In Probrachylophosaurus, the frontals covering the nasal articulation cover only about 59% of the frontal bone, compared to full coverage in adult Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: While in adult Brachylophosaurus these cover the entire top of the frontal to support the longer crest, in Probrachylophosaurus they only cover around half of the frontal (59% coverage).

facts.statement: The quadrate bones in Probrachylophosaurus are straight in shape, unlike those in Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura where the top half leans backward.
facts.quote: The left and right quadrate form the rear corners of each side of the skull. In Probrachylophosaurus and Acristavus the quadrates are straight in shape, whereas the top half leans backward in Brachylophosaurus and Maiasaura.

facts.statement: In Probrachylophosaurus, the opening for cranial nerve VII is slightly behind and below the opening for cranial nerve V, differing from the arrangement in Acristavus.
facts.quote: A key feature of these genera is the opening for cranial nerve VII, which is slightly behind and below that for cranial nerve V rather than directly behind it as in Acristavus.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Probrachylophosaurus exhibited variation between slender and robust crest morphologies between individuals, as seen in Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: Whether the crest varied between “slender” and “robust” morphologies between individuals, as in Brachylophosaurus, is unknown.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus is classified as a hadrosaur within the solid-crested subfamily Saurolophinae and the tribe Brachylophosaurini.
facts.quote: Probrachylophosaurus is a hadrosaur, belonging to the solid-crested subfamily Saurolophinae (alternatively Hadrosaurinae) and specifically to a lineage known as Brachylophosaurini.

facts.statement: Later phylogenetic analyses suggest Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus are close relatives, excluding Maiasaura from their immediate lineage.
facts.quote: All later phylogenetic analyses would support the latter interpretation, wherein Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus are close relatives to the exclusion of Maisaura.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus, Brachylophosaurus, and Ornatops are united by a specific anatomy of the frontal and nasal sutures that supports a wide, backward-projecting head crest.
facts.quote: The former three are united by the anatomy of the suture of the frontals and nasals, which consists of long striations along the frontals expanded backwards to support the wide, backward projecting head crest known from Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus (and inferred to be present in Ornatops).

facts.statement: Researchers considered Ornatops to be a possible intermediate form in brachylophosaurin evolution, having a nasofrontal suture expansion between that of Probrachylophosaurus and Brachylophosaurus.
facts.quote: It was considered possible that Ornatops, whose nasofrontal suture is expanded more than Probrachylophosaurus but less than Brachylophosaurus, represented an intermediate form in brachylophosaurin evolution

facts.statement: It remains debated whether the relationships between Probrachylophosaurus, Brachylophosaurus, and Ornatops are complicated by independent evolution of the nasofrontal suture expansion in Ornatops.
facts.quote: Thus, the possibility the relationships between these taxa are more complicated and that nasofrontal suture expansion may have occurred independently in Ornatops were not ruled out.

facts.statement: While Brachylophosaurini lineages were replaced in North America by the middle Campanian, the group persisted in Asia into the Maastrichtian, as evidenced by the genus Wulagasaurus.
facts.quote: Brachylophosaurini, along with Kritosaurini, would go on to be replaced by the lineages Saurolophini and Edmontosaurini through the middle Campanian and into the Maastrichtian in North America, though Brachylophosaurini would persist in Asia as shown by the Maastrichtian genus Wulagasaurus.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Probrachylophosaurus, designated MOR 2919, exhibits several injuries including depressions on the dentaries and texturing on the leg bones.
facts.quote: MOR 2919, the type specimen of P. bergei, shows several injuries.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of the type specimen MOR 2919 indicates that Probrachylophosaurus reached an age of fourteen years at death.
facts.quote: In the tested specimen of Probrachylophosaurus MOR 2919, fourteen LAGs indicated the animal was fourteen years of age at death.

facts.statement: The head crest of Probrachylophosaurus experienced significant growth very late in the animal's life history, unlike the rest of its skeleton.
facts.quote: Unlike the rest of the body, the display crest on the top of the head experiences much of its growth very late in the life history of the animal.

facts.statement: Sexual maturity in the Probrachylophosaurus specimen MOR 2919 appears to have been reached at five years of age.
facts.quote: In MOR 2919, this appears to happen at five years of age.

facts.statement: A 2026 study concluded that injuries to the mid-tail neural spines in Probrachylophosaurus were most likely caused by mating mechanisms rather than predation or other factors.
facts.quote: A 2026 study found the mating mechanism to be most likely and ruled out the other hypotheses as failing to explain the pattern of damage seen across hadrosaurs specimens.

facts.statement: Probrachylophosaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous period.
